clue.text: Bird lay at back of pub

indicators.note: the wager is placed behind the pub word, so it comes after it in the answer

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
to lay money on something is to bet, and a bet is a lay

explanation.surface: A bird lays an egg out behind the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' tempts as egg-laying, but here it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbets are squat, colourful tropical birds related to toucans.

clue.text: Swimmer shows sparkle keeping amazingly fit

indicators.note: the sparkle word holds the other letters within it, as a box keeps its contents

parts.note: a flash is a sudden sparkle of light

indicators.note: the word fit is treated in an amazing, astonishing way, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A swimmer shows off a sparkling, remarkably fit physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is crossword shorthand for a fish; 'amazingly' scrambles the fodder into ATFI, which 'keeping' places inside the sparkle word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice or sole is a fish, and so a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Crooked type caught in the act

indicators.note: the type word is trapped inside the act word, as a thief caught in the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
a form is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A dishonest sort is caught red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in the act' reads as one idiom, but 'caught in' is the container and 'the act' gives DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bent out of its proper shape is misshapen, which is what crooked means here.

clue.text: Supreme warrior seen by worker as big bully

parts.note: Tyr is the Norse god of war, a supreme warrior figure
an ant is a worker in the usual crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A top fighter, standing beside a labourer, looks like a great bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, the ultimate domineering person.

clue.text: Plants I left in lounges?

indicators.note: the I and the left letter are set inside the lounges word

parts.note: to lie about is to lounge, so lounges gives lies

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to leave the plants in the sitting rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounges' looks like a noun for rooms but is the verb 'lies' (lazes).
explanation.definitionFit: Lilies are flowering bulbous plants.

clue.text: Female slave who has won the affection of a spy?

definitions.text: who has won the affection of a spy?
definitions.meaning: read as one of the women of the film spy James Bond, a maid belonging to him

explanation.surface: A slave girl wins the heart of a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: James Bond, the fictional British spy, has many girlfriends in the films.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondmaid is an old word for a female serf or slave girl.

clue.text: Rescuer showing kindness, lovable person

parts.note: grace can mean kindness or favour
a darling is a lovable person

explanation.surface: A lifesaver shows kindness and is a real sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling was a lighthouse keeper's daughter famed for rescuing shipwreck survivors off Northumberland in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian heroine rowed out in a storm to save stranded sailors.

clue.text: Peculiar lens distorted astronomical phenomenon

indicators.note: the letters are twisted out of shape, as a warped lens distorts an image

explanation.surface: An odd, warped lens produces a strange sight in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges PECULIAR and LENS together.
explanation.definitionFit: When Earth's shadow falls on the moon, that eclipse is a celestial event.

clue.text: Bits of wax, maybe — sort mostly used for warm coat

parts.note: seals are pieces of wax pressed onto letters, among other kinds

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: kind means sort

explanation.surface: Wax pieces of a certain kind go into making a cosy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts KIND to KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelts of seals were made into fur garments for cold weather.

clue.text: Boy embracing the girl will be beaten

indicators.note: the boy word wraps its arms round the girl word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A lad hugging his girlfriend fears a thrashing will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashed means whipped, struck repeatedly with a cord or cane.

clue.text: Song and dance created by a small daughter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
D is the abbreviation, a small form, for daughter

explanation.surface: A little girl puts on a song-and-dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like one phrase; 'Song' is the definition and 'and' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or slow sentimental tune.

clue.text: Note a bit botched conveys Parisian's parting message

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly written note carries a Frenchman's farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges NOTE, A and BIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'see you soon', said when taking leave of someone.

clue.text: Auntie prepared endless food for insects

parts.note: Auntie and the Beeb are both nicknames for the BBC

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: An aunt cooks up a never-ending meal for bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, is nicknamed 'Auntie' and 'the Beeb'. 'endless' turns READY into READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees store pollen as a food for their larvae, known by this name.

clue.text: Course consisting of Greek food

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A meal course made up of Greek dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford University honours course in classics, ancient history and philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a university degree programme, a course of study at Oxford.

clue.text: Bloomer maybe made by a mum hugging priest

indicators.note: the mother word wraps round the priest word

parts.note: ma is a mother, a mum
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A mother cuddles a clergyman and a mistake is made.
explanation.walkthrough: Amelia Bloomer, a US campaigner, popularised the women's trousers called bloomers; 'maybe' marks her as one Bloomer among others.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia was the first name of the dress reformer Mrs Bloomer.

clue.text: Spooner's dispatching delivery in station area

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening letters change places

parts.note: in cricket, a batsman hooking the ball sends it away to leg
a ball is a bowler's delivery in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone muddles their words about sending off a delivery at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a hook is an attacking shot dispatching a short delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket office at a railway station is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Holiday arrangement by fast mover

parts.note: in arithmetic, three by four means three times four
a hare is a fast-running animal

explanation.surface: A speedy traveller makes holiday plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is the multiplication sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint ownership of a holiday home, each owner using it for set weeks.

clue.text: Tale going round in our time that could die out

indicators.note: the tale word goes round the era letters

parts.note: a fable is a tale
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A story circulating today might soon be forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to fade can wither away, disappearing over time.

clue.text: Protein that's doin' somethin'

definitions.meaning: a muscle protein that works with myosin
acting with its g dropped, in the clue's dropped-g style, means doing something

explanation.surface: A protein busy at work, as a casual speaker puts it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes in the clue signal the dropped G of the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Actin is one of the two proteins that make muscles contract.

clue.text: Tree not easily moved? Get rid of root

indicators.note: in a down clue the root is the bottom letter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: firm means solid, not easily shifted

explanation.surface: A tree is hard to shift, so dig out its root.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the bottom letter is the word's 'root', so M is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir is a coniferous evergreen tree.

clue.text: Feeling conveyed that is not lacking heart

parts.note: sent means conveyed
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken away, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Emotion is shown, which proves someone is not heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' takes the O out of NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means capable of feeling or sensation.

clue.text: Alas, men face being whipped for illegal act

indicators.note: whipped like cream, the letters are beaten into a new form

explanation.surface: Men regret facing a flogging for their crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being whipped' rearranges ALAS, MEN and FACE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Malfeasance is wrongdoing, especially by an official.

clue.text: A quiet friend, Heather can be awful

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
a pal is a friend
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken pal called Heather can be dreadful company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling means shockingly bad, dreadful.

clue.text: Training gets union support on course, having admitted delay

parts.note: TU stands for trade union

indicators.note: the support word lets the delay word in, holding it

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball on a golf course
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A trade union backs a training course despite a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a training course, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guidance from a teacher.

clue.text: Rope put down, wrapped round man to be lifted

indicators.note: the landing word encloses the turned man

parts.note: to land something is to put it down

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word turns it upward, reading it backwards

parts.note: Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A rope is laid down and wound round someone to haul him up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to be lifted' turns the man upward, giving YAR, which 'wrapped round' encloses; 'put down' is the landing verb, not a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, especially on a ship.

clue.text: Religious people who are wicked not half exposed

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: devils are wicked people
out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: Pious folk are said to be wicked, though not entirely shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps DEV from DEVILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout means deeply pious, devoted to religion.

clue.text: Anchor sank finally landing on something sharp?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter sits on top of the second piece
the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an edge, as of a blade, is sharp

explanation.surface: An anchor sank, finally coming to rest on a jagged point.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedge is a small anchor used to warp a ship along.

clue.text: Hit up ball in the middle

indicators.note: only the central part of the word is used, with both ends dropped

parts.note: a globe is a ball

explanation.surface: Someone smashes the ball high from the centre of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' keeps the inside of GLOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to hit a ball high into the air.
